documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2025-01-16.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson is doing well on replacement for primary adrenal insufficiency. Energy and strength are much improved and he has regained weight, now 80 kg. No illnesses requiring stress dosing so far. Pigmentation is lighter.

BP 116/72. Sodium and potassium normal on today's BMP.

Plan: continue hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg early afternoon, and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Emergency kit in date. Review sick-day rules annually. See us in about a year, sooner as needed.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel 3/18 f/u, work deployment that week. Feels fine. Offered reschedule; he'd rather fold it into his physical in May. Physical confirmed 5/20.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47M, annual.

Feels the best he has in a couple of years. Back to normal workdays, walking at lunch again.

Adrenal insufficiency: hydrocortisone 15/5, fludrocortisone 0.1. Endo Jan, no changes, next visit in a year. No stress doses needed. Wears his med alert bracelet.
Sarcoidosis: no cough, no skin lesions. Pulm said return as needed.
Chronic anemia: no symptoms.

Meds: hydrocortisone 10 mg 1.5 tab qAM, hydrocortisone 5 mg 1 tab early afternoon, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily, hydrocortisone 100 mg IM kit prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP and weight reviewed, weight back up to 81. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft, NT. Skin: residual faint darkening of palmar creases. Shins clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. Repeat PSA (shared decision, he prefers to keep checking).
2. Adrenal insufficiency: stable on replacement.
3. Sarcoidosis: quiescent.
4. Anemia: trend.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.2, stable for him. CMP normal incl Na/K. A1c, lipids normal. PSA 0.9. Released to portal with comment.

medications.sig: Apply thin layer to affected area twice daily for 2-4 weeks

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit. Rash on lower abdomen for about 3 weeks. Itchy and sore, worse with sweat and the waistband. Tried an OTC clotrimazole cream and then OTC hydrocortisone cream for about a week each, neither helped much. No fever.

On video and uploaded photo: red, scaly patch across the lower abdomen below the umbilicus, edges somewhat sharper than the center.

A/P: Likely intertrigo/fungal given location, summer, sweat. Rx ketoconazole 2% cream BID, keep area dry, loose waistband. If not clearly better in 3-4 weeks, come in so I can look in person.

medications.sig: Apply thin layer to affected areas twice daily for up to 2 weeks; avoid the face

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rash f/u. Five weeks of ketoconazole, no real change, now spreading down into the groin. Painful more than itchy. Weight 78.5, down from 81 in May; he says he's been skipping lunch with a big project and not very hungry.

Exam: afebrile. Erythematous scaly patches lower abdomen extending to inguinal folds bilaterally, some crusting at edges. No vesicles. No satellite pustules.

A/P: Not behaving like tinea. Stop ketoconazole. Trial of triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID x 2 wk in case this is an eczematous/irritant process. If no better, dermatology. Recheck weight next visit.

orders.reason: Painful rash of lower abdomen, groin and perineum not responding to topical antifungal and steroid

documents.title: Rash still bad
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The steroid cream calmed it for a few days but it came right back and now it's spread back toward my bottom. It burns. Can I see a dermatologist? I've attached two pictures.

documents.title: RE: Rash still bad
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the photos, Jamal. Yes, this needs a dermatologist, and I've put the referral in today. Stop the triamcinolone in the meantime. Our front desk will call you with the appointment. If you get a fever or the skin opens up and drains, let me know right away.

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology referral sent with notes and photos. First new-patient opening 10/14. Pt accepted, waitlisted for sooner.

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, left medial thigh at edge of plaque, 4 mm punch.
Microscopic: epidermis with confluent parakeratosis and pallor of the upper spinous layer with scattered necrotic keratinocytes. Superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis. PAS stain negative for fungal elements.
reports.conclusion: Necrotic keratinocytes in the upper epidermis with perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate; no fungal organisms. See comment: in the right clinical setting the pattern is compatible with necrolytic migratory erythema.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice. Seen 2025-10-14.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Mr. Robinson, 47, who carries diagnoses of sarcoidosis and primary adrenal insufficiency on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. NKDA.

He has had a painful rash for four months that began on the lower abdomen and has moved into the groin and perineum despite several antifungal and steroid creams, none of which helped for long. He has lost about 8 kg over the past three months without trying, feels more tired, and has some mild abdominal discomfort. He has also had a dry mouth and been more thirsty lately, which he puts down to stress.

Exam: weight 73 kg. A large red, scaly plaque with crusted areas and central clearing across the lower abdomen and onto both medial thighs. Mild pallor of the conjunctivae.

Labs today: hemoglobin 10.2 with normocytic indices, glucose 212, ALT 64 and AST 52. HIV screen negative.

A punch biopsy was taken from the edge of the thigh plaque.

Impression: chronic, treatment-resistant eruption of the lower abdomen, groin and perineum with weight loss, anemia and hyperglycemia. I am concerned about necrolytic migratory erythema and will write again with the pathology.

With thanks,
Dermatology

documents.title: Dermatology Addendum
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice.

Dear Doctor,

The biopsy shows necrotic keratinocytes high in the epidermis with a perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate and no fungus. With the clinical picture of a migrating flexural rash, weight loss, anemia and a glucose of 212, this is most consistent with necrolytic migratory erythema.

Necrolytic migratory erythema is classically a sign of a glucagon-secreting pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. I would recommend a serum glucagon level and dedicated pancreatic imaging. I called Mr. Robinson today to explain and told him your office would be in touch.

With thanks,
Dermatology

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm letters reviewed. Called pt, booked 10/20 AM, fasting. Will order glucagon and pancreas-protocol CT at that visit.

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast, pancreas protocol
orders.reason: Necrolytic migratory erythema, evaluate for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u derm. Biopsy + clinical picture read as necrolytic migratory erythema; derm recommends glucagon and pancreatic imaging to look for a glucagonoma.

Rash about 4 months: lower abdomen -> groin -> perineum. Painful. Weight 81 in May, 78.5 Aug, 73 at derm, 72.8 today. Tired, mild vague abdominal discomfort. Dry mouth and thirsty for a few weeks. Glucose 212 at derm. ALT 64 / AST 52, Hgb 10.2. Taking hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone as prescribed, no extra doses.

Exam: thin compared with spring. Mild conjunctival pallor. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass or organomegaly. Skin: large scaly erythematous plaque lower abdomen into the inguinal folds and medial thighs with crusted edges.

A/P
1. Necrolytic migratory erythema with weight loss, hyperglycemia and anemia: glucagon level today, CT abd/pelvis pancreas protocol ASAP. Discussed with him plainly that this pattern can come from a hormone-producing pancreatic tumor; he asked good questions, wife on speaker.
2. Hyperglycemia: very likely part of the same process, on top of daily hydrocortisone. Not labeling diabetes yet, holding off on meds pending workup. Repeat CMP today. He'll call for polyuria worsening, vomiting or confusion.
3. Adrenal insufficiency: same doses. Emailed endo with derm findings so they're in the loop before any procedure.
4. Mildly elevated LFTs: recheck today, CT will look at liver.
5. Flu + COVID today.

Call with any questions.

documents.title: Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with glucagon 1,180 pg/mL (ref 50-150), markedly elevated. Fits the derm concern. CMP from 10/20: glucose still high, LFTs similar. CT booked 10/28. He understands the next step is finding where the tumor is. Spent 15 min.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Technique: multiphase CT of the abdomen with pancreatic protocol (late arterial and portal venous phases) and portal venous imaging of the pelvis after IV contrast. Indication: elevated glucagon, necrolytic migratory erythema.
Findings: There is a 3.4 x 2.9 cm solid mass in the pancreatic tail that enhances avidly in the arterial phase. The pancreatic duct is not dilated. The remainder of the pancreas is normal. Liver: no focal lesions. Gallbladder and bile ducts normal. Spleen normal in size. Adrenal glands unremarkable. Kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis. No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy. No ascites. Bowel unremarkable; appendix surgically absent. Lung bases clear. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: 3.4 cm arterially enhancing solid mass of the pancreatic tail, in the setting of elevated glucagon most consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (glucagonoma). No hepatic lesions or adenopathy.

documents.title: Imaging Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT: 3.4 cm hypervascular pancreatic tail mass, no liver lesions or nodes. With glucagon 1,180, this is a glucagonoma until proven otherwise. Will call pt tomorrow AM when I can talk it through properly; refer surgical oncology.

documents.title: CT Results Discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Phone with pt and wife. Reviewed CT: single 3.4 cm mass in the tail of the pancreas, no sign of spread to liver or lymph nodes. Explained this is very likely the glucagon-producing tumor driving the rash, weight loss and high sugars, and that surgery is usually the treatment when it's localized like this. Referral to surgical oncology placed, urgent. Endo updated. He was quiet but appreciated the call; wants everything moving. Couldn't reach him yesterday, LVM.

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Surgical oncology referral faxed with CT report, glucagon and derm letters. Consult scheduled 11/13 1:00 pm. Pt notified.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2025-11-06.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the update on Mr. Robinson. The elevated glucagon and pancreatic tail mass make a glucagonoma the working diagnosis, and he has a surgical oncology consultation next week.

Adrenal insufficiency: stable, same hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone doses. For surgery he will need stress-dose coverage: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV at induction, then 50 mg IV every 8 hours, tapering back to his usual oral doses over two to three days as he recovers. I have sent this to the surgical team.

Hyperglycemia: I expect this to improve after the tumor is removed. With resection the likely next step, we agreed to watch it without starting a medication; he knows the symptoms that should prompt a call.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Outside surgical oncology clinic. Seen 2025-11-13.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Robinson, 47, with a 3.4 cm arterially enhancing pancreatic tail mass, serum glucagon of 1,180 pg/mL and biopsy-supported necrolytic migratory erythema. Background: primary adrenal insufficiency on replacement, sarcoidosis, chronic anemia, remote appendectomy. NKDA.

Exam: thin, otherwise well. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed right lower quadrant scar. Skin findings as described by dermatology.

Imaging shows localized disease without hepatic involvement.

Recommendation: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy. We discussed risks including pancreatic leak, bleeding, infection and conversion to open surgery. He wishes to proceed; surgery is planned for 12/9.

Pre-operative needs:
1. Vaccination against encapsulated organisms at least two weeks before surgery: pneumococcal conjugate and meningococcal ACWY. We would be grateful if your office could give these.
2. Stress-dose steroids per his endocrinologist's plan.

With thanks,
Surgical Oncology

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pre-splenectomy vaccines per surgical oncology letter and PCP order; surgery 12/9 (3 wk). Afebrile, no acute illness. No prior vaccine reactions.
Given: PCV20 L deltoid; MenACWY R deltoid. VISs provided.
Observed 15 min, no reaction. MenACWY dose 2 due in 8 weeks or more: flagged for February visit. Pt has wallet card listing doses.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, surgical oncology service.
Admitted 2025-12-09. Discharged 2025-12-12.

Procedure: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy, 2025-12-09. No conversion. Estimated blood loss minimal. Drain placed at the pancreatic stump.

Indication: 3.4 cm pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor with markedly elevated glucagon and necrolytic migratory erythema.

Hospital course: Stress-dose hydrocortisone 100 mg IV at induction, then 50 mg IV every 8 hours on POD 0-1, reduced on POD 2 and back to his home oral hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone on POD 3. Hemodynamically stable throughout. Clear liquids POD 1, regular diet POD 2. Drain amylase low; drain removed POD 3. Glucose readings fell into the 100s-120s after resection without insulin. Pain controlled on oral medication. Ambulating independently.

Allergies: NKDA.

Discharge medications: hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg early afternoon; fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily; hydrocortisone 100 mg IM emergency kit; oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 one tablet every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, 12 tablets.

Asplenia: pre-operative vaccines given 11/18 at his PCP's office. MenACWY dose 2 due in February. Advised to seek care promptly for any fever.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; surgical oncology clinic in 6 weeks with repeat glucagon; final pathology to follow.

documents.title: Operative Note
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Procedure: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal. Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV given at induction.
Findings: firm, well-circumscribed mass in the pancreatic tail without invasion of adjacent structures. Liver surface smooth, no visible lesions. No peritoneal disease. Spleen normal in appearance.
Technique: five ports. Lesser sac entered, splenic flexure mobilized. Pancreas divided proximal to the mass with a stapler; splenic artery and vein controlled. Specimen extracted in a bag through an extended port site. Drain left at the stump.
Complications: none. Specimen to pathology.

reports.text:
Specimen: distal pancreas and spleen.
Gross: distal pancreas 9.0 cm with a well-circumscribed tan mass in the tail measuring 3.4 cm, 1.2 cm from the closest parenchymal margin. Attached spleen 11.0 cm, unremarkable cut surface.
Microscopic: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor with nested and trabecular architecture, uniform nuclei, no necrosis. Mitoses fewer than 2 per 2 mm2. Ki-67 index 2%. Immunohistochemistry: synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; glucagon positive in tumor cells. No lymphovascular or perineural invasion. Parenchymal and vascular margins negative. Eleven peripancreatic lymph nodes negative (0/11). Spleen without pathologic change.
reports.conclusion: Distal pancreas: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, WHO grade 1 (Ki-67 2%), 3.4 cm, glucagon immunopositive, margins negative, 0/11 lymph nodes; no lymphovascular invasion. Spleen: unremarkable.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Final path reviewed: WD NET G1, glucagon+, 3.4 cm, margins neg, 0/11 nodes. Good result. Will review with him at Thursday's post-discharge visit.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Lap distal pancreatectomy + splenectomy 12/9, home 12/12. Path: WD NET G1, glucagon+, 3.4 cm, margins neg, 0/11 LN.

Recovering. Pain mostly with getting up from bed, took 4 of the oxycodone tabs total, none in the last 3 days. Eating small meals, appetite returning. BMs normal. No fever. Back on usual hydrocortisone 15/5 and fludro 0.1 since POD3. Thirst gone. Rash already less angry, burning much better.

Meds reconciled with discharge list: no changes besides short oxycodone course.

Exam: afebrile. Port sites clean, dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near extraction site. Skin: groin and lower abdominal plaque paler, less scale.

A/P
1. S/p distal pancreatectomy/splenectomy for glucagonoma: healing well. Surg onc f/u 1/22 with repeat glucagon.
2. Asplenia: PCV20 and MenACWY #1 given 11/18; MenACWY #2 at Feb visit. Counseled fever = same-day call or ED. Will need meningococcal boosters going forward; flagged.
3. Hyperglycemia: glucose today much better. Recheck in Feb.
4. Adrenal insufficiency: tolerated stress dosing, back on home doses.
5. Weight 71. Expect regain.
